Prehistory: Period of human history before records.
Ascending the Siamese throne in 1782 following the deposition of King Taksin, this monarch became the first ruler of the Chakri dynasty and founded the city that is now Bangkok — who was he?
Rama I: King of Siam from 1782 to 1809.
A Labour politician who served two decades on the Kensington and Chelsea council, she also worked as a senior lecturer at Kingston University — who is she?
Rima Horton: English former councillor and economics lecturer (born 1947)
From 1904 to 1905, two empires clashed over rival ambitions in Manchuria and Korea, fighting major naval battles in the Yellow Sea and the Sea of Japan — which war was this?
Russo-Japanese War: 1904–1905 conflict in East Asia.
Inspired by a 4th-century Greek bishop known for secret gift-giving, this white-bearded, red-suited figure is said to deliver presents by sleigh on Christmas Eve — who is he?

Santa Claus: Legendary Christmas figure. Santa Claus is a legendary figure originating in Western Christian culture who is said to bring gifts during the late evening and overnight hours on Christmas Eve.
Named after the TV show in which its founder played a fictional president, this Ukrainian political party has ruled since Volodymyr Zelenskyy won the presidency in 2019 — which party?
Servant of the People: Political party in Ukraine. It was formed in late 2017 and was officially registered on 31 March 2018 on the basis of the previously registered Party of Decisive Changes.
Ruling from 893 to 927, this monarch's campaigns against the Byzantines and Magyars brought the First Bulgarian Empire to its greatest size and a cultural Golden Age — who was he?
Simeon I of Bulgaria: First Emperor of the Bulgars from 893 to 927.

Before the Civil War he taught at the Virginia Military Institute; historians rank this Confederate general among the most gifted tacticians in U.S. history, and he died in 1863 from wounds in the war's eastern theater — who was he?
Stonewall Jackson: Confederate States Army general (1824–1863)
A former actor turned anti-establishment politician, this Japanese lawmaker founded a party called Reiwa Shinsengumi and once ran for Tokyo governor — who is he?
Taro Yamamoto: Japanese politician and former actor.
Coregent with his stepmother Hatshepsut for 22 years before ruling alone, this pharaoh led between 17 and 20 victorious military campaigns that brought Egypt's empire to its peak — who is he?
Thutmose III: Pharaoh of Egypt from 1479 to 1425 BC.
The second Rashidun caliph and a father-in-law of the prophet Muhammad, he once set out to kill Muhammad with his sword before a spiritual break led him to convert in 616 — who was he?
After her newspaper-publisher husband was assassinated, she took over La Prensa and went on to become Nicaragua's first female president. Who was she?
Violeta Chamorro: President of Nicaragua from 1990 to 1997.
He began his career studying geology in Gansu before rising to become Premier of China from 2003 to 2013 — which retired Communist Party leader?
Wen Jiabao: Premier of China from 2003 to 2013. Born in Tianjin, Wen joined the Chinese Communist Party in 1965.
Born a Lithuanian polytheist and known as Jogaila as Grand Duke, he converted to Catholicism in 1386, married Queen Jadwiga, and became sole ruler of Poland — who was he?
Władysław II Jagiełło: Grand Duke of Lithuania (1377–1434); King of Poland (1386–1434)
This late-Qing statesman raised and organized the Xiang Army to crush the Taiping Rebellion and helped launch the Tongzhi Restoration — who was he?
Zeng Guofan: Chinese politician and military commander (1811–1872)
Which one below was born first?
Mikhail Lomonosov (born 1711) is the earliest of the four. One of the founders of modern geology, Lomonosov was also a poet and influenced the formation of the modern Russian literary language.
Which of these people was born first?
Zhuge Liang (born 181) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four began earliest?
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four. It is named after French mathematician, philosopher and physicist Blaise Pascal.
Pick the astronomer from these four.
Galileo Galilei is an astronomer. Galileo has been called the father of observational astronomy, modern-era classical physics, the scientific method, and modern science.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Blaise Pascal is a mathematician. Blaise Pascal (19 June 1623 – 19 August 1662) was a French mathematician, physicist, inventor, philosopher, and Catholic writer.
What is the atomic number of Unbinilium?
Unbinilium, also known as eka-radium or element 120, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has symbol Ubn and atomic number 120.
What is the atomic number of Arsenic?
Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
In what year was Ted Kaczynski born?
Ted Kaczynski: The FBI used the case identifier UNABOM (University and Airline Bombing) before his identity was known, resulting in the media naming him the "Unabomber".
In what year was Steve Wozniak born?
Steve Wozniak: In 1976, he co-founded Apple Computer (now Apple Inc.) with his early business partner Steve Jobs.
In what year was Dmitri Mendeleev born?
Dmitri Mendeleev: The synthetic element mendelevium is named in his honor.
In what year did Ptolemy die?
Ptolemy: The first was his astronomical treatise now known as the Almagest, originally entitled Mathēmatikḗ Syntaxis (Μαθηματικὴ Σύνταξις, 'Mathematical Treatise').
In what year did Al-Khwarizmi die?
Al-Khwarizmi: Few biographical details are known about al-Khwarizmi's life.
In what year was Nitrogen discovered?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
Which company manufactures Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk?
Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk: Skunk Works. It was the first operational aircraft to be designed with stealth technology.
In which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21 based?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21: Soviet Union. Approximately 60 countries across four continents have flown the MiG-21, and it still serves many nations seven decades after its maiden flight.
Who is credited with discovering Triangulum Australe?
Triangulum Australe: Américo Vespucio. Triangulum Australe is a small constellation in the far Southern Celestial Hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Ichthyosaurus?
Ichthyosaurus: Mary Anning. It is among the best known ichthyosaur genera, as it is the type genus of the order Ichthyosauria.
Who is credited with discovering Theobroma cacao?
Theobroma cacao: Christopher Columbus. Theobroma cacao (cacao tree or cocoa tree) is a small (6–12 m (20–39 ft) tall) evergreen tree in the Malvaceae family.
Who is credited with discovering Krypton?
Krypton: William Ramsay. Krypton (from Ancient Greek: κρυπτός, romanized: kryptos 'the hidden one') is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

A German-born theoretical physicist best known for developing the theory of relativity, his mass–energy formula E=mc2 comes from special relativity and has been called "the world's most famous equation." Born in 1879, who won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics?
Albert Einstein (14 March 1879 - 18 April 1955) was a German-born theoretical physicist best known for developing the known theory of relativity.
Whether from too few red blood cells or faulty hemoglobin, this disorder leaves the blood less able to carry oxygen — often felt as quiet tiredness long before any paleness shows — what is it?
Anemia (also spelt anaemia in British English) is a blood disorder in which the blood has a reduced ability to carry oxygen.

A German former computer repair technician, this man received international attention after murdering and cannibalizing a voluntary victim he had found over the Internet in March 2001, and was ultimately convicted of murder in a 2006 retrial — who is he?

Armin Meiwes (born 1 December 1961) is a German former computer repair technician who received international attention for murdering and cannibalising Bernd Brandes, whom he had found via the Internet as a voluntary victim, in March 2001.
Only eight species of this stocky-legged, shaggy, short-tailed carnivoran survive, ranging across North and South America and Eurasia — what mammal is it?
Bear are carnivoran mammals of the family Ursidae.
This insect order contains both cockroaches and termites — the latter now classified as a specialized, social lineage within the former group — what order is it?
Blattodea is an order of insects that contains cockroaches and termites.
Affecting roughly 22% of people worldwide and often striking during sleep, this parafunctional habit grinds teeth and clenches jaws until enamel wears away — what's it called?
Bruxism is excessive teeth grinding or jaw clenching.

This American astronomer and planetary scientist was initially an assistant professor at Harvard before moving to Cornell as the David Duncan Professor of Astronomy. He played an active role in the Voyager programs. Who is he?
Carl Sagan (November 9, 1934 - December 20, 1996) was an American astronomer, planetary scientist and science communicator.

Once prized as refrigerants and aerosol propellants — Freon being the famous example — these halogenated compounds were phased out under the Montreal Protocol for gnawing holes in the ozone layer — what are they?
Chlorofluorocarbon (CFCs) and hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs) are fully or partly halogenated hydrocarbons that contain carbon (C), hydrogen (H), chlorine (Cl), and fluorine (F).
In mathematics, this term describes a selection of items from a set in which the order of choosing doesn't matter — unlike its counterpart, the permutation. Name the concept?
Combination is a selection of items from a set that has distinct members, such that the order of selection does not matter (unlike permutations).

This practice and field of study focuses on techniques for secure communication in the presence of adversaries, sitting at the intersection of mathematics, computer science, and electrical engineering — what's the field called?
Cryptography is the practice and study of techniques for secure communication in the presence of adversarial behavior.
A colorless liquid that's a workhorse solvent for chemical reactions, this compound is officially odorless — yet degraded samples reek of fish thanks to a dimethylamine impurity; what is it?
Dimethylformamide is an organic compound with the chemical formula HCON(CH3)2.
Despite common belief, this shocking South American fish belongs to the knifefish order and is more closely related to catfish than its name implies — what is it?
Electric eel are a genus, Electrophorus, of neotropical freshwater fish from South America in the family Gymnotidae, of which they are the only members of the subfamily Electrophorinae.
This sweet-tasting but toxic diol is a workhorse of antifreeze and polyester manufacturing, and astronomers have even detected the molecule in space — what is it?
Ethylene glycol (IUPAC name: ethane-1,2-diol) is an organic compound (a vicinal diol) with the formula (CH2OH)2.
Encompassing everything from oral tales and proverbs to festival rituals and traditional building styles, what term describes the shared expressive culture of a group?
Folklore is the body of expressive culture shared by a particular group of people, culture or subculture.
Ordained a priest in 1923, this Belgian physicist connected an expanding universe to Einstein's field equations and floated an early Big Bang hypothesis — who was he?
Georges Lemaître (lə-MET-rə; 17 July 1894 - 20 June 1966) was a Belgian Catholic priest, theoretical physicist, and mathematician who made major contributions to cosmology and astrophysics.

This German physicist turned his eye on the mind itself, founding psychophysics and giving his name to a law showing that sensation rises with the logarithm — not the raw intensity — of a stimulus. Whose pioneering work was it?
Gustav Fechner (19 April 1801 - 18 November 1887) was a German physicist, philosopher, and experimental psychologist.
Sometimes called urticaria, this itchy rash of raised welts can flare for minutes or days, may follow an allergy or infection, and in half of all cases has no identifiable cause — what is it?
Hives is a kind of skin rash with red or flesh-colored, raised, itchy bumps.

For decades this University of Virginia psychiatrist ran a Division of Perceptual Studies and gathered evidence that memories — and even bodily features — might carry across lives. Which researcher into reincarnation was he?

Ian Stevenson (October 31, 1918 - February 8, 2007) was a Canadian-born American psychiatrist, the founder and director of the Division of Perceptual Studies at the University of Virginia School of Medicine.
This Canadian-American physical educator invented an entire sport, wrote its original rule book after moving to the United States, and founded the University of Kansas's program in 1898 — who is he?
James Naismith (November 6, 1861 - November 28, 1939) was a Canadian-American physical educator, physician, Christian chaplain, and sports coach, best known as the inventor of the game of basketball.
One species of this succulent plant genus, native mainly to Madagascar, became one of the first plants ever sent into space aboard a Soviet space station in 1979 — what genus is it?
Kalanchoe (also called "kalanche" or "kalancho"), is a genus of about 125 species of tropical, succulent plants in the stonecrop family Crassulaceae, mainly native to Madagascar and tropical Africa.
Closely related to earthworms but equipped with a sucker at each end, these segmented parasitic or predatory worms make up their own subclass within the annelid phylum — what are they?
Leech are segmented parasitic or predatory worms that comprise the subclass Hirudinea within the phylum Annelida.
Based on a commercial airliner design, this four-engine turboprop aircraft hunts submarines for the U.S. Navy using a distinctive tail-mounted magnetic detector — what plane is it?
Lockheed P-3 Orion is a four-engined, turboprop anti-submarine and maritime surveillance aircraft developed for the United States Navy and introduced in the 1960s.

With over 2,400 species sporting triangular heads, bulging eyes on flexible necks, and folded forelegs built to snatch prey, these insects count termites and cockroaches among their closest relatives — what are they?
Mantis are an order (Mantodea) of insects that contains over 2,400 species in about 460 genera in 33 families.
Sold dissolved in solution or shipped anhydrous in pressurized railcars, this simplest primary amine reeks like rotten fish — what compound is it?
Methylamine is an organic compound with a formula of CH5N or CH3NH2.
Containing antimicrobial lysozymes and immunoglobulins, most of this protective body fluid is produced in the gastrointestinal tract — what is it called?
Mucus is a slippery fluid produced by, and covering, mucous membranes.
Also called niacin, this organic compound is an essential vitamin B3 that plants and animals produce from the amino acid tryptophan. What is it?
Nicotinic acid is an organic compound and a vitamer of vitamin B3, an essential human nutrient.
This flowering herb in the mint family, native to the Mediterranean, is sometimes called wild marjoram and is a staple of countless savory dishes. What is it?
Oregano (Origanum vulgare) is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae.
Which American biologist became famous for the controversial 1968 book 'The Population Bomb' and its dire warnings about population growth, famine, and resource depletion?

Paul R. Ehrlich (May 29, 1932 - March 13, 2026) was an American biologist, author, and environmentalist known for his predictions and warnings about the consequences of population growth, including famine and resource depletion.

Derived from phosphoric acid by removing one to three protons, this anion or salt takes forms like dihydrogen and hydrogen variants and gives its name to fertilizers and various esters — name the ion?
Phosphate is an anion, salt, functional group or ester derived from a phosphoric acid.
This spiny rodent actually comes in two unrelated varieties, an Old World family and a New World family, whose lookalike coats of keratin quills evolved independently — what animal is it?
Porcupine are large rodents with coats of sharp spines, or quills, that protect them against predators.
This opening at the center of the iris lets light reach the retina and appears black — round in people, a slit in cats, and even a ring shape in some catfish — what's it called?
Pupil is a hole located in the center of the iris of the eye that allows light to strike the retina.

One of the rarest and most valuable precious metals, this hard, corrosion-resistant transition metal with only one naturally occurring isotope is prized for enhancing jewelry — what's the element (symbol Rh, atomic number 45)?
Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
Also known as Besnier-Boeck-Schaumann disease, this non-infectious condition causes inflammatory cell clusters called granulomata, most often striking the lungs, skin, or lymph nodes — what is it?
Sarcoidosis is a non-infectious granulomatous disease involving abnormal collections of inflammatory cells that form lumps known as granulomata.

This medical state of insufficient blood flow to body tissues comes in four main types, from hypovolemic to cardiogenic, and can progress from weakness and rapid breathing to confusion or cardiac arrest. What is this condition called?
Shock (circulatory) is the state of insufficient blood flow to the tissues of the body as a result of problems with the circulatory system.

Some versions allow a 'tie' or 'draw' while others insist on a single winner; it can pit hundreds against each other or just one person against the clock — what do we call this organized physical activity?
Sport is a physical activity or game, often competitive and organized, that maintains or improves physical ability and skills.
Down, Wolf–Hirschhorn, and Andersen–Tawil are all named examples of this medical term for a cluster of correlated signs and symptoms — what is it?
Syndrome is a set of medical signs and symptoms which are correlated with each other and often associated with a particular disease or disorder.
This American economist and social theorist, a prominent voice in the conservative movement, received the National Humanities Medal from President George W. Bush in 2002 — who is he?
Thomas Sowell (SOHL; born June 30, 1930) is an American economist, economic historian, and social theorist.

Entering Soviet service in the 1960s, this jet was the USSR's first supersonic bomber to reach production, though it disappointed with poor range and proved notoriously hard to fly — what aircraft is it?
Tupolev Tu-22 (Air Standardization Coordinating Committee name: Blinder) was the first supersonic bomber to enter production in the Soviet Union.

Many of these carrion-eating birds sport a bald head that stays clean while feeding and helps with temperature control — and they'll even urinate on their own legs to cool off. What kind of bird is it?
Vulture is a bird of prey that scavenges on carrion.
Each individual's coat is unique, and the best evidence suggests their black-and-white pattern wards off biting flies — which striped African equine is this?
Zebra (subgenus Hippotigris) are African equines with distinctive black-and-white striped coats.
Located behind the nasal cavity where the nose meets the throat, which mass of lymphoid tissue is also known as the pharyngeal tonsil?
Adenoid: Type of tonsil. The adenoid, also known as the pharyngeal tonsil, or nasopharyngeal tonsil is the superior-most of the tonsils.

Born out of wedlock in the Caribbean and orphaned young, this Founding Father became the first U.S. secretary of the treasury and started America's first political party, the Federalist Party — who was he?
This memory disorder comes in two main forms — one blocking recall of events before a specific date, the other preventing new experiences from becoming lasting memories — what is it?
Amnesia: Cognitive disorder where memory is disturbed or lost.
Shed and regrown every year on most male deer, this bony head growth serves as both a weapon and a symbol of sexual attraction — what is it?
Antler: Skull projections found in deer.
Dubbed the 'Prophet of the Space Age,' this English science fiction author co-wrote the screenplay for 2001: A Space Odyssey and formed sci-fi's 'Big Three' with Heinlein and Asimov — who is he?
Arthur C. Clarke: British science fiction writer (1917–2008)
With six species native to Africa (and one also found in Arabia), these large Old World monkeys have dog-like muzzles and have existed for at least two million years — what are they called?
Once chairman of the Nasdaq, this financier admitted to masterminding the largest-known Ponzi scheme in history, estimated at $65 billion — who is it?
Bernie Madoff: American financier and con artist (1938–2021)
Announced in 2011, this fourth-generation narrow-body jet introduced more efficient LEAP engines and split-tip winglets, with variants from the 7 up through the 10 — what aircraft is it?
Patented by Roche in 1961 and approved for medical use in 1974, which benzodiazepine, similar in effect to diazepam, is sometimes given as a presurgical sedative in 1.5, 3, or 6 mg tablets?
Bromazepam: Benzodiazepine drug. Bromazepam, sold under many brand names, is a benzodiazepine.
First synthesized in 1950 by bombarding curium with alpha particles, this actinide element bears the symbol Cf and is named for a US university and state — what is it?
Californium: Chemical element with atomic number 98 (Cf)
This corvid, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic, is stockier and larger than its North American cousin but nearly identical in appearance — what bird is it?
Carrion crow: Species of bird. The carrion crow (Corvus corone) is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic.
In a joint presentation with Alfred Russel Wallace, this English naturalist unveiled the idea that the struggle for existence drives a process he likened to selective breeding — who was he?
Charles Darwin: English naturalist and biologist (1809–1882)
This genus native to South and Southeast Asia gave rise to oranges, lemons, and limes through extensive hybridization — what is it?
This icy wanderer of the solar system grows a gassy halo and sometimes a tail stretching more than an astronomical unit as it nears the sun — what is it?
Comet: Natural object in space that releases gas.

First published in 1785 by a French physicist, this principle holds that the electrostatic force between two charged particles is proportional to their charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them — which principle is it?
Coulomb's law: Fundamental physical law of electromagnetism.

Originally bred for the hunt and later famous for trotting alongside horse-drawn firehouse carriages, this white breed with dark spots traces its roots to a region on the Adriatic coast — which breed?
Dalmatian dog: Croatian hunting/carriage/coach dog breed.
Approved for medical use in the US back in 1950, this medication treats intestinal spasms such as those seen in irritable bowel syndrome — what is it called?
This first section of the small intestine, often the principal site of iron absorption, connects the stomach to the middle portion of the intestine — what is it?
Duodenum: First section of the small intestine. The duodenum is the first section of the small intestine in most vertebrates, including mammals, reptiles, and birds.
This German chess player, mathematician and philosopher held the world title for 27 years — the longest reign ever — partly by a famously "psychological" approach to rattling opponents; who was he?

This branch of zoology studying animal behavior traces its scientific roots to Darwin and came into its own in the 1930s through Nobel laureates Tinbergen, Lorenz, and von Frisch — what's the field called?
First described from a skull in 1846 and initially mistaken for a porpoise, this highly social oceanic dolphin gets its common name from a skull resembling that of the orca — which species?
False killer whale: Species of oceanic dolphin in the genus Pseudorca.
Discovered in Dubna in 1999, this superheavy synthetic element (number 114) honors a Russian physicist whose name in Cyrillic explains why its spelling swaps a 'yo' for an 'e' — which element?
Flerovium: Chemical element with atomic number 114 (Fl)
This Canadian physician and author has written five books linking childhood trauma to conditions like ADHD and addiction, though critics question the evidence behind some claims — who is he?
The only venomous lizard native to the United States, this sluggish reptile from the Southwest rarely poses a real threat despite its fearsome reputation — what is it?
Gila monster: Largest species of lizard in the United States.

Despite its name, this marine reptile's shell ranges from olive to black — its nickname actually comes from the color of the fat beneath its carapace, built up from an all-plant diet — which species is this?
Green sea turtle: Species of large sea reptile. The dorsoventrally flattened body of C. mydas is covered by a large, teardrop-shaped carapace; it has a pair of large, paddle-like flippers.

Made by fusing heavy nuclei in tiny quantities, this superheavy element 108 has a special isotope whose "magic numbers" of protons and neutrons make its deformed nucleus unusually stable — what is it?
Hassium: Chemical element with atomic number 108 (Hs)
Hardy enough to survive winters as cold as -43°C, this shrub genus's aggressive roots fight soil erosion, and its berries and leaves are turned into food and skincare products — which genus?
Hippophae: Genus of flowering plants including sea buckthorn.
This Greek-derived name means 'thin skin' and refers to a piece of mucosal tissue that partially covers the vaginal opening in many mammals — which structure?
Hymen: Membrane that surrounds or partially covers the vaginal opening.
Symbolized by the '∞' sign and debated by philosophers since ancient Greece, this endless concept was later shown by Georg Cantor to come in different sizes when applied to sets. What is it?
Infinity: Mathematical concept. Infinity is something which is boundless, limitless, or endless.
This neo-Keynesian economist gave his name to a model for censored data — the 'tobit' — while advising the Fed and championing government action against recessions; who is he?
James Tobin: American economist and Nobel Laureate (1918–2002)
While tinkering with electromagnets, this American physicist discovered self-inductance and went on to become the very first secretary of the Smithsonian Institution — who was he?
Joseph Henry: American physicist and inventor (1797–1878)
The largest joint in the human body, it's a modified hinge that links the thigh to the lower leg via two separate joints — what is it?
Knee: Leg joint in primates. The knee is a modified hinge joint, which permits flexion and extension as well as slight internal and external rotation.
This Hungarian-born physicist conceived the nuclear chain reaction in 1933, then drafted the letter Einstein signed that launched the Manhattan Project — who was he?
Leo Szilard: Hungarian-American physicist and inventor (1898–1964)

Born from a 1970s Skunk Works project to dodge Soviet missile defenses, this subsonic single-seat attack jet became the first operational aircraft ever designed around stealth technology, first flying in 1981 at Groom Lake — which aircraft is it?
Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk: American stealth ground-attack aircraft.

Founder of the Kerala school, this Indian mathematician was the first to use infinite series to approximate trigonometric functions — a 'decisive step' toward the limit-passage to infinity; who is he?
Madhava of Sangamagrama: Indian mathematician and astronomer (1340–1425)
Growing out of calculus and the study of derivatives and integrals, this branch of mathematics examines functions, spaces, and limits using methods of approximation and convergence — which field?

Mathematical analysis: Branch of mathematics. Mathematical analysis is the branch of mathematics that studies functions, spaces, and operators through quantitative methods of approximation and convergence.
This scientific field studies the atmosphere and short-term weather phenomena, with applications spanning aviation, agriculture, and disaster management — what field is it?
Meteorology: Scientific study of the atmosphere focusing on weather forecasting.
This Israeli-American physician turned billionaire donor owns the Las Vegas Review-Journal and Dallas Mavericks, and was one of Donald Trump's largest financial backers — who is she?

Miriam Adelson: Israeli-American physician, billionaire, and conservative donor. Miriam Adelson (née Farbstein; born October 10, 1945) is an Israeli-American physician, businesswoman, philanthropist, and conservative political donor.
This Austrian-School economist founded anarcho-capitalism and called the state "the organization of robbery systematized and writ large" — which libertarian theoretician?
The sole species in its genus and a fixture of Mediterranean gardens, this drought-and-flood-tolerant shrub of the dogbane family is also called rose laurel or rosebay — what is it?
Nerium: Species of plant. It is the only species currently classified in the genus Nerium, belonging to subfamily Apocynoideae of the dogbane family Apocynaceae.
Built from a nitrogen-containing base, a five-carbon sugar, and a phosphate group, these molecules are the monomer building blocks of DNA and RNA — what are they called?
Nucleotide: Biological molecules constituting nucleic acids.

Believed to be the world's fourth-leading cause of disability, this degenerative joint disease comes from the breakdown of cartilage and bone, often striking the fingertips, thumb base, knees, and hips — what is it?
Osteoarthritis: Form of arthritis caused by degeneration of joints.
Known as the passion flower, this genus of about 550 species also has ornamental hybrids that have won Royal Horticultural Society awards and varieties used in ayahuasca analogs — name the genus?
Passiflora: Genus of flowering plants in the passion flower family.
Known online by the alias 'brokep,' this Swedish-born entrepreneur co-founded a famous BitTorrent search engine before launching the privacy-focused registrar Njalla in 2017 — who is he?
Peter Sunde: Swedish entrepreneur and politician. Peter Sunde Kolmisoppi (born 13 September 1978), alias brokep, is a Swedish-born Finnish-Norwegian entrepreneur and politician.
Also called threadworm in the UK and seatworm elsewhere, this common intestinal roundworm spreads via the faecal-oral route and is especially prevalent among children — what parasite is it?
A purplish-black crystalline salt that dissolves into an intensely pink-to-purple solution, this strong oxidizer also appears on the WHO's List of Essential Medicines for wound care — what is it?
The earliest vertebrates known to achieve powered flight, these warm-blooded Mesozoic reptiles had wings stretched from ankle to a dramatically lengthened fourth finger — what were they called?
Pterosaur: Extinct order of flying reptiles.

A pioneer in optical character recognition and speech synthesis, this futurist inventor received the National Medal of Technology from President Clinton in 1999 for his outlook on AI and life extension — who is he?
Ray Kurzweil: American computer scientist, author and futurist (born 1948)
Often called the first modern chemist, which 17th-century Anglo-Irish natural philosopher described the inverse relationship between a gas's pressure and volume in a law that bears his name?
Named for the genus of the Atlantic salmon, this family of cold-water fish also includes trout, char, and grayling — what family is it?
People with this anxiety disorder are fully capable of speech but fall silent in specific situations or around specific people, even when staying quiet brings shame or punishment — what is it called?
Selective mutism: Anxiety disorder blocking speech. Selective mutism usually co-exists with social anxiety disorder.
This layer of tissue covering a vertebrate's body serves three main functions: protection, regulation, and sensation?
Skin: Soft outer covering organ of vertebrates.

First described in 1915 by a German paleontologist from Egyptian fossils that were destroyed during World War II, this dinosaur genus wasn't represented by new material until the early 2000s — which genus?
Spinosaurus: Genus of spinosaurid dinosaur. The genus was known first from Egyptian remains discovered in 1912 and described by German palaeontologist Ernst Stromer in 1915.
The first variable-sweep-wing aircraft to enter Soviet service, this fighter-bomber was produced from 1967 to 1990 and exported in variants flown across the Arab world — which jet?
Sukhoi Su-17: Soviet variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber. The Sukhoi Su-17 (Russian: Су-17; NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
The lone living family within its primate infraorder, these small Southeast Asian mammals favor forests thick with liana vines, which give them vertical support as they climb — which animal?
The body's primary muscle of respiration, this dome-shaped sheet separates the chest cavity from the abdomen and contracts to pull air into the lungs — what is it?
Thoracic diaphragm: Sheet of internal skeletal muscle.
